title: Barren plateaus in quantum neural network training landscapes
problem_summary: Shows that for a broad class of reasonably expressive parameterized quantum circuits (including VQE ansatze), the variance of the cost-function gradient vanishes exponentially with system size, so gradients become exponentially small ('barren plateaus') almost everywhere in a randomly-initialized parameter landscape -- a foundational trainability-limitation result that motivates several other corpus entries (e.g. ostaszewski2021, kulshrestha2024, grimsley2023).
sources_verified: referenced via multiple corroborating secondary sources in this search pass; DOI/venue/article-number independently corroborated across them

components.family_or_name: gradient-variance scaling analysis for random circuit initialization
components.notes: Theoretical result, not a proposed ansatz/optimizer itself -- establishes a trainability constraint that other corpus papers explicitly try to mitigate.

workflow_composition_notes: Not a VQE workflow paper itself; a foundational analysis of why randomly-initialized, sufficiently-expressive VQE-style ansatze become untrainable at scale, motivating adaptive-growth (ADAPT-VQE family) and RL-guided (ostaszewski2021) alternatives to random initialization.
